discovery: Programmable quantum matter with individually controlled Rydberg atoms: Rydberg blockade entanglement and optical-tweezer arrays for quantum simulation

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: The nominees turned the strong dipole-dipole interaction between Rydberg atoms into a controlled resource for building quantum matter atom by atom. Lukin proposed the Rydberg blockade as a mechanism for fast neutral-atom quantum gates; Saffman and Browaeys (with Grangier) observed blockade between two individually trapped atoms in 2009 and used it to entangle them. Browaeys then pioneered defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms in optical tweezers, and Browaeys and Lukin used them to realise quantum Ising and XY magnets, topological spin liquids, quantum many-body scars and programmable logical qubits. These are superbly controlled experiments on single quanta, in which patient instrument-building has yielded genuinely new insight into strongly correlated quantum dynamics, measurement and entanglement. Rydberg arrays now stand beside trapped ions and superconducting circuits as a leading platform for quantum simulation and computation, and have opened a new area of many-body physics.
